title: I made a free background remover web app using 6 cutting-edge AI models
author: fyrean

comments.author: fyrean
comments.body:
I understand the challenge of meticulously removing backgrounds from images, especially when dealing with flowing hair. That's why I created this tool so anyone can remove backgrounds from images and videos for free! Choose from six cutting-edge removal methods. You can even remove the sky from landscape photos. Get creative!

This web app runs directly in your browser, so there's no need for downloads or installations.  
[fyrean.itch.io/bgbye-background-remover](https://fyrean.itch.io/bgbye-background-remover)

I'm planning to release the source code soon, once I clean it up and add even newer models (e.g., ormbg). Note that hosting the server locally requires at least 12GB of RAM and a GPU with at least 8GB of VRAM (more if you want to rmbg larger images). A CPU-only version will also be available in the future.

There are many use cases for this tool. For instance, you can generate game characters and items using stable diffusion and remove the background to display them over your own game backgrounds. You can also create videos using Lumalabs, and since the generated videos are opaque, this tool can help you remove the background with ease.

replies.author: Drakim
replies.body:
Looks great!

One issue I've always with all these kinds of tools is that even though the background is cut out, a sort of colored halo still remains around the character. I can even see it in your example, especially around the hair. Is there any good method for trimming away it without doing it by hand?

replies.author: fyrean
replies.body:
there are more models I've yet to try! Especially SAM models that allow you to specify exactly what you want to segment (keep). Lets see if they work better on hair...

As for manually removing the background around the hair... When i do it by hand I erase the separated strands of hair along with the background, so the final result doesn't have any of the separated strands of hair. But thankfully 90% of the time at least one of the model can expertly remove the background from all of the hair regions so I don't have to resort to that.

comments.author: FireyDeath4
comments.body: Today I looked for a bunch of online background removers, and the one I ultimately settled on was Clipping Magic, because I needed to control the boundaries between what was considered the subject and background since the subject and background were rather specific and ambiguous. It only lets you access small previews for free, but I worked around that by uploading crops that were smaller than the maximum preview size. It has a keep tool that forces painted areas to be interpreted as the subject, a remove tool that forces them to be interpreted as the background, a hair tool that processes things on clean and distinct backgrounds with lots of holes or differences like strands of hair, tree branches, and even gradients like shadows and some forms of noise, a scalpel tool focused on sculpting specific boundaries in cases where there's poor contrast, and various processing modes and ways of refining edges. These would be some handy additions to your program if you're interested in adding them
